title: Machine learning optimizes carbon dot synthesis for Co2+ and Cu2+ nanosensors
summary: Neural-network and regression models predicted Co2+ and Cu2+ concentrations from carbon dot photoluminescence excitation-emission matrices, with test mean absolute error 0.55 mM (Co2+) and 0.62 mM (Cu2+). Error maps against synthesis parameters gave optimal hydrothermal conditions of citric acid:ethylenediamine 1:2, 150-155 C and 210-230 min, which the authors report were validated experimentally. The work covers a single sensor system, and improvement over standard synthesis was not assessed in this review.
ai_technology: CNN models (one per carbon-dot type), TL_S-MLP and LR/GB regressors predicting ion concentrations; error-vs-synthesis-parameter models to select synthesis conditions

evidence.tested: Held-out test spectra gave the stated errors, and the ML-derived optimal synthesis conditions were experimentally validated per the paper.
evidence.unknown: Improvement versus standard synthesis and performance beyond this single sensor system were not read.
evidence.ai_role: Predicted ion concentrations from spectra and identified synthesis conditions that minimize prediction error.

source_review.scope: Full text and author affiliations read via Europe PMC metadata for this DOI.
